title: Texans vs. Chargers Live Score & Stats: November 8, 2026 GameTracker Update – CBS Sports
body:
Houston’s defense finally got the payoff it has been chasing all season, forcing a late‑game turnover that helped the Texans edge the Los Angeles Chargers 24‑20 on Sunday night in a thriller that swung back and forth until the final minutes. Quarterback C.J. Stroud, who battled flu‑like symptoms all week, delivered a gritty performance that reminded fans of Michael Jordan’s legendary “Flu Game,” throwing for 312 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a crucial third‑quarter score. The victory snaps a three‑game losing streak for Houston and keeps its wild‑card hopes alive, while the Chargers’ playoff aspirations are now in jeopardy as they fall to 5‑5.

The contest began with the Chargers asserting early dominance, capitalizing on a miscue by the Texans’ special teams unit that gave Los Angeles a short field. Rookie wide receiver Jaxon Smith caught a 28‑yard touchdown pass from veteran starter Justin Herbert, putting the Chargers ahead 7‑0 within the first five minutes. Houston responded quickly, however, as Stroud, despite feeling under the weather, orchestrated a methodical drive that culminated in a 12‑yard touchdown pass to tight end Dalton Schultz. The early exchange set the tone for a back‑and‑forth battle, with both offenses finding rhythm while the defenses struggled to make decisive stops.

Midway through the second quarter, Houston’s defense began to find its footing. Defensive end Jalen Carter, returning from a minor ankle sprain, recorded his first sack of the season, bringing down Herbert on a third‑down play and forcing a three‑and‑out. The momentum shift was palpable; the Texans forced a fumble on the ensuing drive, recovered by safety J.J. Wilcox, who returned it to the Chargers’ 32‑yard line. Stroud capitalized, connecting with wideout Jordan Addison on a 45‑yard strike that set up a short rushing touchdown by running back Dameon Pierce. The Texans took a 14‑7 lead into halftime, a lead they would cling to despite a late‑quarter surge by Los Angeles.

The second half saw the Chargers adjust their offensive scheme, employing more quick slants and screen passes to neutralize Houston’s pass rush. Herbert, displaying his veteran poise, engineered a 70‑yard drive that culminated in a 19‑yard touchdown pass to veteran receiver Keenan Allen, tying the game at 14‑14. The Chargers then took their first lead of the night with a field goal early in the fourth quarter, making it 17‑14. Yet Stroud, still battling chills and fatigue, refused to yield. On a crucial third‑down conversion, he scrambled for 22 yards, extending the drive and eventually finding Schultz again for a 7‑yard touchdown that restored Houston’s lead at 21‑17.

The final minutes were a study in high‑pressure football. With just under two minutes left, the Chargers drove deep into Houston territory, and a well‑timed pass interference call placed them at the 5‑yard line. Herbert’s subsequent pass into the end zone was intercepted by cornerback Derek Stingley Jr., who returned it to the Chargers’ 35‑yard line. The Texans capitalized on the turnover, with Stroud delivering a short pass to running back Zay Jones for a 12‑yard gain that set up a decisive 32‑yard field goal by rookie kicker Cameron Dicker, sealing the 24‑20 win.

Beyond the scoreboard, the game highlighted several broader narratives. Stroud’s resilience under physical duress could cement his status as a future league MVP, while the Chargers’ reliance on Herbert’s arm underscores the need for a more balanced rushing attack if they hope to stay competitive in a tightly contested AFC West. Houston’s defense, long criticized for inconsistency, finally showcased the playmaking ability that made them a top‑10 unit on paper, suggesting that a healthier roster could translate into a late‑season surge.

Looking ahead, the Texans travel to Denver next week to face the Broncos, a matchup that could determine whether they remain in the wild‑card conversation. If Stroud can stay healthy and the defense continues its upward trajectory, Houston may well finish the season as a surprise playoff contender. For the Chargers, a win against the Kansas City Chiefs will be essential to keep their postseason dreams alive, and they will need to address the offensive line’s protection issues that were exposed in the final minutes against Houston. Both teams now stand at a crossroads, with the next few weeks likely to define the remainder of their 2026 campaigns.
